stem: Inaya and Boman each start with the same whole chapati. Inaya cuts hers into $4$ equal pieces. Boman cuts his into $4$ pieces of different sizes. Each takes one piece and calls it one-fourth of the chapati.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides whose piece is a valid one-fourth?

options.text: Only Inaya's piece is one-fourth, because the whole was split into equal-size parts.
Both pieces are one-fourth, because each person took one of four pieces.
Calling a piece one-fourth is what forces the chapati cuts to be equal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A fractional unit needs equal-size parts of the identified whole; only Inaya's equal cuts give a true one-fourth.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal-size partitioning of the whole makes a valid unit fraction. Counting four pieces of any size omits equal size. Saying the name creates equal cuts reverses the relation.
